As a talent manager, I've seen my fair share of headshot sessions. And let me tell you, the difference between a "meh" photo and a showstopper often comes down to the makeup (or lack thereof). Yes, you read that right – for child actors, less is almost always more. But achieving that "naturally flawless" look requires some strategic know-how. I’ve noticed a unique challenge with teenage girls. Despite their love for makeup in daily life, it’s crucial to dial it back for headshots. Convincing them can be a bit of a tussle, but trust me, the ‘less is more’ approach pays off in front of the camera.

A recent parent question post in our facebook community Child Actor 101 prompted me to break it down in a blog post.

So, parents, put away the glitter and stage makeup – we're going for fresh-faced confidence under the camera.

Here's a breakdown of what to focus on:

Prepping the Canvas:

  • Hydration is king (or queen!): A well-moisturized face reflects light beautifully. Choose a fragrance-free, lightweight moisturizer suitable for your child's skin type. Product Tip: CeraVe Baby Daily Lotion is a gentle, non-greasy option for sensitive skin.

  • Tame the shine: Oily patches can create unwanted glare. A light dusting of loose powder will balance things out without looking cakey. Product Tip: Laura Mercier Loose Setting Powder is translucent and finely milled, perfect for young skin.

Enhancing Features:

  • Brows on point: Neatly groomed brows frame the face and add expression. Avoid over- tweezing; use a spoolie brush to comb hairs into place and a clear brow  gel to set them. Product Tip: Benefit Gimme Brow Volumizing Eyebrow Gel adds a touch of definition without looking unnatural.

  • Kiss the dark circles goodbye: Under-eye circles can make your child look tired. A tiny dot of concealer that matches their skin tone can work wonders, but use it sparingly. Product Tip: NARS Radiant Creamy Concealer offers good coverage without weighing down the skin.

  • A touch of rosy charm: Cream blush adds a healthy flush to the cheeks. Apply a small amount to the apples of their cheeks and blend well. Product Tip: Glossier Cloud Paint is a sheer, buildable gel-cream blush that comes in a range of natural shades.

  • Lashes with a flutter: Mascara opens up the eyes and adds sparkle. Clear is best but you can opt for a brown or black mascara, depending on your child's hair color, and focus on the upper lashes. Skip the liner – it can be aging for younger kids. Product Tip: Benefit They're Real! Lengthening Mascara lengthens and defines without clumping.

  • Naturally kissable lips: Skip the gloss! A clear lip balm or a light-colored lip tint will keep lips hydrated and add a subtle hint of color. Product Tip: Burt's Bees Tinted Lip Balm is available in a variety of barely-there shades and provides nourishing moisture.

Remember:

  • Less is truly more. The goal is to enhance your child's natural beauty, not mask it.

  • Don't forget the sunscreen! Even studio lights can be harsh on young skin. Choose a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher sunscreen suitable for sensitive skin. Product Tip: La Roche-Posay Anthelios Clear Skin Dry Touch Sunscreen SPF 60 is lightweight, oil-free, and won't clog pores.

Teen-Focused Tips:

  • Teenage girls often have their own makeup preferences. Acknowledge their style but explain the difference between everyday and camera-ready makeup.

  • Find a middle ground to compromise. If they insist on more makeup, agree on subtle enhancements. For instance, a very light touch of mascara or a natural-toned eyeshadow.

  • Education the teenagers. Explain how heavy makeup can age them on camera or distract from their natural features, which isn’t ideal for child actor headshots.

Bonus Tips:

  • Practice makes perfect! Let your child get comfortable with the makeup routine beforehand.

  • Encourage them to express themselves! Their confidence and personality will shine through in the photos.

  • Most importantly, relax and have fun! Capturing their natural energy is what makes a great headshot.

By following these tips and choosing the right products, you can help your child achieve that effortlessly flawless look for their next headshot session. Remember, the goal is to showcase their natural beauty and keep them looking as young as possible. 

P.S. If you're feeling overwhelmed, consult a professional makeup artist who specializes in child actors. They can offer personalized recommendations and ensure your child feels comfortable and confident on camera.
